# Hwanung walks into a solar & renewable energy firm

Somewhere right now, in a solar & renewable energy office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Hwanung**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Descent from Heaven.** Yearning to rule the world below, Hwanung asked his father Hwanin to send him to earth.  Hwanin granted him three heavenly seals and three thousand retainers, and Hwanung descended to a sandalwood tree on the slopes of a high mountain.

**The Rule of Wind and Rain.** Hwanung governed the natural forces that sustain agriculture: wind, rain, clouds, and grain.  Under his rule the people learned the arts of civilisation, including law, medicine, and the weaving of cloth.

## Not the First Rebrand

Hwanung functions as a culture-hero in the Korean mythic system, comparable to other East Asian figures who descend from heaven to teach agriculture and law.  The story has been read through Confucian, Buddhist, and Daoist lenses, each tradition finding in it a model of virtuous rule or cosmic harmony. The office is only the latest translation.
